solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worthy Lib Dem minister embraces right change

indicators.note: the minister's name holds the following pieces within it, as arms embrace

parts.note: Vince Cable was a Liberal Democrat cabinet minister
to edit a text is to change it

explanation.surface: A deserving Liberal Democrat politician welcomes reform of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable, a Liberal Democrat Business Secretary in the UK coalition government, supplies the outer letters, split after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creditable deserves praise, so it is worthy in the sense of being estimable.

clue.text: King facing death to become torn

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A monarch faces execution and the nation is split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just places R in front of END.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend, used intransitively, is to split or be torn apart, as cloth does under strain.

clue.text: What may be swept under the carpet at uni results in quarrel

parts.words: What may be swept under the carpet
parts.note: dirt hidden by a lazy cleaner is dust
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Concealed dirt in a student house leads to a row.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to university and are up while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust-up is an informal word for a fight or noisy argument.

clue.text: Horrible mist restricts our travel business

indicators.note: the scrambled letters close in around the next word, hemming it in
something horrible is a mess, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dreadful fog is limiting the holiday trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' looks like a comment on the weather; it signals the jumble, and 'restricts' has the jumbled fog hem in the possessive word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is the industry of organising and serving holidays and visitors.

clue.text: Tempt player at the crease — one will get caught

indicators.note: the piece named is trapped inside the other, as a ball is caught

parts.note: the batsman at the crease in cricket is a bat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cricketer is lured into a shot and gets caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line where a batsman stands in cricket; BAT is a crossword word for a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait is to lure or entice, as a hook is baited to tempt a fish.

clue.text: Not vacant, waiting for the match?

definitions.meaning: a toilet or phone line in use is occupied
a couple betrothed are waiting for their marriage, a match

explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means both occupied, as a lavatory sign shows, and promised in marriage.

clue.text: Ghastly nonentities, without love and without feeling

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something horribly mangled, so the letters are rearranged
the zero letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Dreadful nobodies lack affection and show no emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops O from NONENTITIES, and 'Ghastly' rearranges the remaining NNENTITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Insentient means lacking sensation or consciousness, unable to perceive anything.

clue.text: Person in business spoke here, troubled about parking

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation, standing about it
words that are troubled are disturbed, so their letters are mixed

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone at work talked here, worried about where to leave the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges SPOKE HERE, and 'about' puts that around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper runs a retail store, so is one kind of person in business.

clue.text: Sacred symbol engraved in bank house

indicators.note: the letters are cut into the phrase that follows, set within it

explanation.surface: A holy emblem is carved into the wall of a bank building.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the looped cross of ancient Egypt, a symbol of life held sacred.

clue.text: Modest nun is a smug phony

indicators.note: phony means fake, so the letters are given a false arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied nun's humility is just a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassuming describes someone unpretentious who does not push themselves forward.

clue.text: Like fish moving around, then quietly dormant

parts.note: as means like in comparisons

indicators.note: the fish is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Fish swim about, then settle into silent rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like fish' tempts a solver to look for a fishy adjective; 'Like' is a separate piece, and 'moving around' turns only the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep is inactive and at rest, in a dormant state.

clue.text: Being most wet as nuisance clinging to mother

indicators.note: one piece hangs on to the other, sitting right beside it

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a pest is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: A clingy child bothering mum in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampest is the superlative of damp, describing whatever holds the most moisture.

clue.text: Tramp unable to get up and fight

definitions.text: unable to get up and fight
definitions.meaning: a boxer floored and counted out cannot continue

explanation.definitionFit: Down-and-out is a noun for a destitute person and describes a boxer knocked down and out of the fight.

clue.text: Academic study of noted works?

parts.note: noted means written in musical notes, not famous, so the works are compositions

explanation.definitionFit: Musicology is the scholarly study of music, its history and theory.

clue.text: Nominal number all right for being accommodated

indicators.note: the short piece is housed within the number, given lodging there

parts.note: ten is a number
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A figure that is fine to put up as a symbolic amount.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN holds OK to give T-OK-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment is one in name only, nominal rather than substantial.

clue.text: Wee insect — it's a bee possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A small bug is buzzing about: might it be a bee?
explanation.walkthrough: Beastie is Scots for a small creature, familiar from Burns's mouse poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish speech a beastie is a little creature, often an insect or bug.

clue.text: Roll in satchel with meal mum brought out

parts.note: a satchel is a type of bag

indicators.note: the letters for mother are taken out of the word before

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: A packed lunch roll in the school bag, with mother taking the food out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' removes M and A from MEAL, leaving EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Simple life form is crazy keeping on

indicators.note: one word holds on to the other inside it

parts.note: mad means crazy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A primitive organism is wildly persistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Monad is a term for a single-celled organism, the simplest unit of life.

clue.text: Knowing characters coming through the airwaves

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the letters are pronounced

parts.note: the letters Y, said as a plural, are characters

explanation.surface: Clever voices are being broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Several letter Ys, said out loud as 'whys', are the characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise means knowledgeable and shrewd, having sound judgment.

clue.text: Express sorrow, having little power

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Grieving in a feeble state.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry tears, the usual outward sign of grief.

clue.text: Gave up church, half-hearted action

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: one of the two central letters is lost from the middle

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Someone quit the church after a feeble gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' takes one E out of the EE heart of DEED, leaving DED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceded means surrendered or handed over, as territory is given up.

clue.text: Small mat for ship

definitions.meaning: a little pad set under a glass
a vessel that trades along a shoreline

explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is both a drinks mat protecting a table and a ship sailing from port to port along the coast.

clue.text: Dim male could create a problem

indicators.note: the letters could be used to make something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stupid man is liable to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a hard choice between two options, a predicament or problem.

clue.text: Bridge warning about to be shifted east

indicators.note: in an across clue east is rightwards, so the letter moves along to the right

parts.note: a caution is a warning
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A card-player's warning about to go East, a bridge seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be shifted east' moves C from the front of CAUTION one place right. Auction bridge is the forerunner of contract bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction is a form of the card game bridge in which players bid for the contract.

clue.text: Boat carrying less cargo?

definitions.meaning: a flat barge used to unload ships
with a smaller load, so of less weight

explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge used for ferrying goods, and lighter means weighing less.

clue.text: Monkey's obvious mistake

definitions.meaning: a loud American primate famous for its call

explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a South American monkey and also a glaring, embarrassing error.

clue.text: Five hundred little folk in digs

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
elves are diminutive folk of legend

explanation.surface: Lots of tiny fairies living in lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like British slang for lodgings, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Delves means digs, literally into earth or figuratively into a subject.

clue.text: Heartless sects in unkind acts

indicators.note: the central letter is removed from the word

parts.note: cults are religious sects

explanation.surface: Uncaring religious groups behaving cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes L, the middle of CULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts are hurtful remarks or snubs, acts meant to wound.

clue.text: Cathedral cleric dismissing chapter immediately

indicators.note: the cleric sends one letter away, so it is dropped

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman on a cathedral staff

explanation.surface: A churchman instantly sacks the cathedral chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral chapter is also its body of canons, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic or literary word for soon or at once.

clue.text: Go round Irish head — finally see beautiful mineral

parts.note: to tour is to go round a place
Malin Head is the northernmost point of Ireland

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: Travel round an Irish headland and finally view a lovely gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline silicate mineral prized as a gemstone in many colours.

clue.text: Desirous impulse evident in return of the grunt

indicators.note: return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are visible inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A yearning shows in a returned grunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'evident' into the definition; it is the hidden-word signal with 'in', leaving 'Desirous impulse' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or impulse to do something.

clue.text: Support character leading national organisation as provider of sustenance

indicators.note: one piece goes in front of the other

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or elbow
aura is a distinctive character or atmosphere
NT is the National Trust, the UK heritage body

explanation.surface: A propping-up role for a figure heading a national body.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is a place serving meals, so it provides people with food.
